title: Can you build lists that meet each mean and median rule?
description: Five conditions on a mean or a median are each met by two lists of numbers. A mean fixes the total, and a median fixes the middle of the sorted list, so many lists can meet one rule.
teaching_notes: One idea: a mean fixes only the total and a median fixes only the middle, so many different lists meet one rule. Watch for students who think each condition has just one answer list.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 2)
video_script.why: A child who can find a missing value from a mean now builds whole lists that meet a mean or median rule.
video_script.substitution: the book's five conditions, each met by two lists of numbers
video_script.anchor: a row of empty boxes ready to be filled with numbers for each condition
video_script.payoff_line: Each condition has two lists that meet it

final_answer.spoken: each condition has two lists that meet it

never_show: a list that does not meet its condition, marked as right
maths_rules: (ii) 4 numbers, median 15.5, middle pair adds to 31: 10, 15, 16, 20 and 1, 15, 16, 99
(iv) 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: total 21, mean 3.5, median (3 + 4) ÷ 2 = 3.5; and six equal numbers such as 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5
(v) 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 7: median 1, total 12, mean 2; and 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 60: median (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7, total 90, mean 15
video_script.design: One row of boxes all video. For each condition the boxes are filled twice, and a total tag or a middle-pair tag shows why the list meets the rule.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the mean and the median. Give two lists of numbers for each of five conditions.
<bookmark mark='one'/>First, three numbers whose mean is eight. Second, four numbers whose median is fifteen point five.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Third, five numbers whose mean is thirteen point six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Fourth, six numbers whose mean equals the median. Fifth, six numbers whose mean is greater than the median. What lists would you give?

beats.on_screen: the condition cards and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a mean fixes the total: total = mean × count; a median fixes only the middle of the sorted list

marks.total: the line total = mean × count appears
marks.mid: the middle of a sorted row is marked, with the other boxes left free

narration: <bookmark mark='total'/>A mean fixes the total, because the total is the mean times the count.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>A median fixes only the middle of the sorted list, so the other numbers are free to change.

beats.on_screen: Given: five conditions on mean and median
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five conditions, each about a mean or a median.

beats.on_screen: To find: two lists for each condition

marks.find: the words two lists for each condition are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two lists for each condition.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Step one, three numbers with a mean of eight need a total of twenty four.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Seven, eight and nine add to twenty four.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four, eight and twelve also add to twenty four.

beats.on_screen: 4 numbers, median 15.5: middle pair adds to 31; 10, 15, 16, 20 and 1, 15, 16, 99

marks.mid: the middle pair of four boxes is marked with the total 31

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step two, four numbers with median fifteen point five. The middle pair must add to thirty one, because the median is their average.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Take ten, fifteen, sixteen and twenty.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Or take one, fifteen, sixteen and ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Step three, five numbers with a mean of thirteen point six need a total of sixty eight.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Ten, twelve, thirteen, fifteen and eighteen add to sixty eight.
<bookmark mark='second'/>One, two, three, four and fifty eight also add to sixty eight.

beats.on_screen: 6 numbers, mean = median: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 has total 21, mean 3.5, median (3 + 4) ÷ 2 = 3.5; also 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5

marks.same: a second row of six 5s appears

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step four, take one, two, three, four, five and six.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>The total is twenty one, so the mean is three point five.
<bookmark mark='median'/>The middle pair is three and four, so the median is three point five too.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Six fives work as well, because every number is the same.

beats.on_screen: 6 numbers, mean > median: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 7 has median 1 and mean 2; 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 60 has median 7 and mean 15

marks.big: one large dot pulls the balance point to the right
marks.first: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 7 fill a row with median 1 and mean 2
marks.second: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 60 fill a second row with median 7 and mean 15

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step five, one large number pulls the mean above the median.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Take one, one, one, one, one and seven. The median is one, and the total is twelve, so the mean is two.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Or take two, four, six, eight, ten and sixty. The median is seven, and the mean is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check two of the lists. Ten, twelve, thirteen, fifteen and eighteen add to sixty eight. Sixty eight divided by five is thirteen point six.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Four, eight and twelve add to twenty four, and twenty four divided by three is eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: both lists work for every condition

marks.ans: the ten lists are boxed in pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each condition has two lists that meet it.
